key_insight: Block sparse spectral optimization has two distinct objectives—A-SUM and A-SQ—with potentially different maximizers; safeguarded A-SQ ascent converges and finitely identifies support under a strict threshold margin.
engineering_relevance: Explicit thresholding and refitting rules make sparse component extraction more reproducible, while local dynamics inform convergence rates and safe screening.
method: Derive A-SUM from normalized loading balls and A-SQ from a quadratic lift.
Establish safeguarded Riemannian ascent convergence using sufficient ascent, relative error, and the Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz property.
Analyze post-identification power and coupled polar maps to characterize local dynamics and derive safe screening.
evidence_signal: Planted-spike tests match predicted identification times and local rates; GPT-2, ViT, and Pitprops panels report PCA-level reconstruction with improved interpretability, while three scRNA datasets show AMI gains of +0.023 to +0.044 over dense PCA at matched sparsity.
watch_item: Convergence guarantees apply to the safeguarded method, not automatically to historical full-polar updates, and finite support identification requires a strict threshold margin.
paper_title: Corrected Block Sparse Spectral Optimization: Exact Models, Finite Identification, and Local Dynamics
